title: Cotangent bootstrap from the diagonal
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Assume that $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(B,B)=0$ for every $i>0$ and that the standard cotangent complex $L_{B/(B\otimes_A B)}$ is zero in the derived category. Then the standard cotangent complex $L_{B/A}$ of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] is zero in $D(B)$.

proof.text: Put $D=B\otimes_A B$, with $\iota_1(b)=b\otimes1$, $\iota_2(b)=1\otimes b$ and multiplication $\mu:D\to B$. Choose a free $A$-module resolution $F_\bullet\to B$. As a bounded-above complex of flat $A$-modules it is K-flat [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], so by [lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit] the derived extension of scalars $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ along $A\to B$ is computed by $F_\bullet\otimes_A B$. Its cohomology in degree $-i$ is $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(B,B)$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], and right exactness of $\otimes$ identifies its $H^0$ with $D$ through the multiplication map. Hence the Tor hypothesis says exactly that the canonical multiplication map $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\to D[0]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-cotangent-flat-base-change] to the commutative square with $C=B$, $A'=B$ (both via the given map $A\to B$), $C'=D$, $C\to C'$ equal to $\iota_1$ and $A'\to C'$ equal to $\iota_2$. Its base-change morphism is a canonical isomorphism $\beta:L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}D\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{D/B}$ in $D(D)$. Here the derived tensor is taken along $\iota_1$, and $L_{D/B}$ is the cotangent complex of $\iota_2$.

proof.text: Apply the canonical transitivity triangle [lem-trf-cotangent-transitivity-triangle] to $B\xrightarrow{\iota_2}D\xrightarrow{\mu}B$, whose composite is $\mathrm{id}_B$. This gives a distinguished triangle $L_{D/B}\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}B\to L_{B/B}\to L_{B/D}\to(L_{D/B}\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}B)[1]$ in $D(B)$, with $L_{D/B}$ the complex of Step 1. The third term is $L_{B/D}=0$ by the hypothesis of the item. For the middle term, [lem-trf-localization-cotangent-vanishing] with $R=B$ and $S=\{1\}$ gives $L_{S^{-1}B/B}=0$. The canonical map $j:B\to S^{-1}B$ is a $B$-algebra isomorphism. The squares from $\mathrm{id}:B\to B$ to $j$ given by $(\mathrm{id}_B,j)$ and back by $(\mathrm{id}_B,j^{-1})$ induce standard maps between $L_{B/B}$ and $L_{S^{-1}B/B}$ [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. Since these maps preserve identities and compose strictly, they are mutually inverse isomorphisms of complexes. Thus every $H^i(L_{B/B})$ vanishes, so $L_{B/B}=0$. In the long exact cohomology sequence of the triangle [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], each $H^i(L_{D/B}\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}B)$ sits between $H^{i-1}(L_{B/D})=0$ and $H^i(L_{B/B})=0$, hence vanishes. So $L_{D/B}\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}B$ is acyclic, that is, zero in $D(B)$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], $L_{B/A}$ is the complex $K=s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/A}\otimes_{P_\bullet}B)$ with $P_\bullet=P^{\mathrm{std}}_\bullet(B/A)$, and $K$ is zero in positive degrees. Each $P_n$ is a polynomial $A$-algebra, so by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] every term $K^{-n}$ is a free $B$-module. Hence $K$ is K-flat [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], and [lem-pc-kflat-scalar-extension-counit] computes $L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}D$, taken along $\iota_1$, as $K\otimes_B D$. That complex also has free terms and is bounded above. By the same two nodes, applying $-\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}B$ along $\mu$ to it is computed by $(K\otimes_B D)\otimes_D B$. Since $\mu\iota_1=\mathrm{id}_B$, the termwise $B$-linear maps $(k\otimes d)\otimes b\mapsto\mu(d)b\,k$ and $k\mapsto(k\otimes1)\otimes1$ are mutually inverse. They commute with the differentials. So $(L_{B/A}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}D)\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}B\cong L_{B/A}$ in $D(B)$. Applying the functor $-\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}B$ to the isomorphism $\beta$ of Step 1 gives $L_{B/A}\cong L_{D/B}\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}B$, which is zero by Step 2. Hence $L_{B/A}=0$ in $D(B)$.
